rationale: Evidence: across 60 development trials (iterations 0, 2 and 3), no run finished. Every run ended off track at progress 0.04 to 0.12, with max error pinned just above the 0.06 m limit and RMS about 0.03 m. Oval and s-bend metrics were identical to three decimal places across base_speed 0.9, 1.3 and 1.6 and across kp 2 to 4 with ki 0 to 0.5. A speed-independent, gain-independent failure at the same progress point suggests the robot leaves the line at a fixed spatial spot, most likely where sensors see the line too late, not because of control dynamics. The sensors sit only 0.04 m ahead of the axle, so the correction starts after the robot is already at the limit. Changes: (1) move sensors forward to y = 0.07 m so they see the line about 3 cm earlier and the correction leads the offset; (2) widen the sensor span to x = -0.05 to +0.05 m with 16 mm footprints so the tape stays under a sensor at larger offsets; (3) keep weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2], which keeps the signal the same order of magnitude; (4) base_speed 1.0, between the 0.9 and 1.3 tests, since speed did not change the failure point. Gains kp 4.0, ki 0.5 and kd 0.6 are kept so that only the sensing geometry and speed move. Expected result: the robot should hold the line through the first bends, with progress above 0.12 and possibly completion. Completion inside 3 s is unlikely at speed 1.0, but staying on track is worth far more. If the robot still exits at the same progress point, the next race should point to the line-loss handling or the wheel mismatch.
